newsitem.title: USA: Sears says cannot tell cost of credit card problem.
newsitem.headline: Sears says cannot tell cost of credit card problem.

text.p: Sears Roebuck & Co said it remains unable to estimate the potential cost of difficulties involving bankrupt Sears credit card holders, the company's handling of them and related legal problems.

"Because Sears is not able to estimate the cost of the matter at this time, no provision has been recorded for it in the first quarter, although it may be material to 1997 operating results," Sears said Thursday.
Sears earlier this month said it exercised "flawed legal judgment" and would refund millions of dollars it collected from bankrupt credit card holders in recent years.

U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Carol Kenner in Boston said Wednesday that Sears had misled many of its bankrupt credit card holders into believing they had to repay their debts to the company, even though those bills were nullified by the bankruptcy court.
Between January 1995 and January 1997, the nation's second-largest retailer used the tactic on more than 2,700 card holders in Massachusetts alone, the judge said.

Sears reiterated Thursday that it has filed a a voluntary nationwide restitution plan regarding the matter. The company also said it was aware that related lawsuits by groups of card holders and Sears shareholders have been filed.
